abstract: Magnesium (Mg{superscript 2}?) homeostasis is essential for parasite survival, yet its transport mechanisms in Plasmodium falciparum remain poorly defined. CorA-family Mg2+ transporters are established targets of cation hexaammines in bacteria, providing a pharmacological approach to investigate CorA-like proteins in malaria parasites. Cation hexaammines exhibited parasiticidal activities, and Co(III)Hex selection yielded a resistant parasite line with an approximately seven-fold increase in IC50 and a substantial growth defect. No coding mutations were detected in PfMIT1, PfMIT2, or PfMIT3; instead, resistance was associated with reduced PfMIT1 and PfMIT2 transcript expression levels. Structural analyses revealed conserved CorA features, including the GMN motif and two C-terminal transmembrane helices. PfMIT1 localized to both the apicoplast and mitochondrion, whereas PfMIT2 and PfMIT3 localized predominantly to the apicoplast. Membrane fractionation further demonstrated distinct membrane-associated states among the three proteins. Collectively, these findings implicate CorA-like Mg{superscript 2}? transporters in parasite biology and identify PfMIT proteins as candidates for antimalarial target development.
